item.title: Apple's 'Welcome Home' event is Tuesday: Home Hub, HomePod Mini 2, new Apple TV 4K
item.description:
Apple's October 13 'Welcome Home' event is shaping up as the company's biggest smart-home moment in years. MacRumors reports the headliner is an all-new Home Hub — a brand-new device category for Apple, not just another speaker — joined by a HomePod Mini 2 with new features and a long-overdue Apple TV 4K refresh.

Six Colors zooms out to ask whether Apple is 'coming home to stay,' arguing this event signals a serious renewed push into the home after years of half-hearted dabbling with HomeKit. If the Hub lands, it would be Apple's first truly new product category since the Vision Pro — with very different stakes. MacRumors' Top Stories roundup collects everything expected so you can walk into Tuesday fully briefed.

item.title: iPhone 18 Pro orders reportedly cut; iPhone Duo will greet owners by name
item.description:
Supply-chain sources claim Apple has cut iPhone 18 Pro orders 'right on schedule' — a rumor that surfaces nearly every iPhone cycle, usually says more about seasonal production adjustments than actual demand, and should be taken with the usual skepticism until sales data arrives.

More concrete: AppleInsider found that the iPhone Duo will greet some owners by name on first boot, a small personal touch in the setup experience that hints at how Apple is thinking about first-run personalization going forward.

Sources

  • AppleInsider: Right on schedule, sources claim iPhone 18 Pro orders have been cut
  • AppleInsider: iPhone Duo will greet some owners by name on its first boot

item.title: Amazon's Alexa Tablet finally gives the iPad real competition
item.description:
9to5Mac argues Amazon's new Alexa Tablet is the first credible iPad challenger in years — and the threat is real precisely because it doesn't try to beat the iPad at Apple's game. Instead it attacks from below with aggressive pricing and an Alexa-first experience.

No Android tablet has managed sustained pressure on the iPad, but Amazon's content ecosystem and smart-home integration give this one a different angle. If it sells, expect Apple to feel pressure to defend the low end of the lineup rather than ceding it entirely.

item.title: Weekend deals: $430 off MacBook Pro M5 Pro, plus AirPods and accessory sales
item.description:
A strong weekend for Apple deals. AppleInsider spots $430 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro, bringing it to $2,069 — one of the steepest discounts on current-gen Pro hardware.

MacRumors rounds up weekend accessory deals spanning TVs, headphones, and smart home gear, while 9to5Mac lists Apple's own weekend sales: AirPods, up to $200 off new Macs, and Apple Watch starting from $41. If you've been waiting on any of these, this is a genuine buy window, not the usual token $20 off.

item.title: Rumor: Apple to announce new partnership with ADT
item.description:
MacRumors reports Apple is set to announce a new partnership with home-security company ADT. Details are thin, but the timing — days before the 'Welcome Home' event — is conspicuous.

An ADT tie-up would give Apple's smart-home push an installed base and professional-monitoring story on day one, rather than asking the Home Hub to bootstrap an ecosystem alone. Expect more partnerships like this if Apple is serious about the home.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Rumor: Apple to Announce New Partnership With ADT

item.title: Odds and ends: 30 Mac minis vs. a Cray-1, macOS 27's underrated IT win, AirPods 5 guide
item.description:
AppleInsider notes that 30 old Intel Mac minis stuffed into a Cray-1 chassis are hugely faster than the supercomputer they live in — a fun reminder of how far commodity computing has come.

For the IT crowd, 9to5Mac highlights remote AppleCare log collection as one of macOS 27's most underrated updates, and its Indie App Spotlight covers Milepost, a driving journal that saves memories from the road. MacRumors also published an AirPods 5 buyer's guide comparing the standard model against the wireless-charging-case version.
